newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends on lows, little impact from sales data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends on lows, little impact from sales data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its lows on Friday after a quiet session where the main focus was on September quarter retail sales data.
A 0.3 percent fall in real, seasonally-adjusted retail sales was in line with expectations and failed to shift the currency or debt markets.
A statement from Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen that the data confirmed a slowing economy and supported the case for an easing also failed to have much impact.

An Auckland dealer said Cullen's statement, the second of its kind in two days, was a case of "the boy who cried wolf". He said the impression was building that nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, was more likely to form a coalition with the caretaker National party government than with Labour after the current protracted negotiations.
"People have decided the longer it goes on, the more likely National will be able to accommodate them (NZ First)," he said.

The market was generally long in the morning, and the currency eased through the session to end at US$0.7100/07 from its opening 0.7120/27. On its Trade-Weighted Index, it slipped to 67.32 from 67.54.
A Wellington dealer concurred the market was "getting a bit immune" to politicians' statements that the currency was overvalued.

He said the kiwi remained supported by underlying investment flows, but the outlook was tempered by political uncertainty and the impression that coalition talks were building towards a resolution. -- Mark Trevelyan 64 4 471-4277
